name: Hot Potato Party Ring
promptTemplate: Hot potato party arena with {{potato_core}} core and {{fuse_speed}} fuse pacing inside a {{arena_glow}} hall, boosted by spark intensity {{sparks_intensity}} and screen shake {{shake_fx}}.

ui.title: HOT POTATO TRAINER
ui.tagline: Pass the core before it detonates in your lap

potato_core.hint: Changes the core shader and flight glow

fuse_speed.hint: Controls fuse countdown duration per round

arena_glow.hint: Switches the stadium backdrop and grid aesthetic

sparks_intensity.hint: Boosts sparks emitted on passes and explosions

shake_fx.hint: Toggles screen shudder on catches and detonations

pass.hint: Fling the glowing potato across the arena

detonate.hint: Instantly blow up whoever is currently holding it

listing.blurb: A fiery glowing orb flings around a ring of players until its timer expires in a flash of smoke, eliminating whoever is caught holding it.
listing.prompt: Hot potato: everyone sits in a ring, and a glowing, ticking potato flies between them; whoever holds it presses 'pass' to throw it to someone else at random; its fuse burns out at a random moment, and whoever holds it then is blackened in a puff of smoke and sits out the next round. Make it a party game a whole room can follow from across the floor: bold shapes and bright colours on a dark ground, every player drawn in their own hue, big short labels (a score, GO!, the winner) in a heavy font, and a large, satisfying reaction on screen the instant anyone presses. It must work with one player or forty, scaling its lanes, seats or pieces to room.people and coping with people joining and leaving mid-round; play itself in a lively attract mode whenever nobody has pressed anything for a few seconds; and after a winner is shown, start the next round on its own. Keep it lean: game state in bounded arrays in room.state, nothing allocated inside hot loops, a steady 60fps at 1920x1080.
